content.description: A Logistics Executive coordinates the day-to-day movement of goods: managing shipment bookings, customs documentation, warehouse handoffs, and carrier/freight-forwarder communication so that orders move on time and within cost. The role sits between hands-on warehouse/transport staff and higher-level supply chain planning, acting as the operational point person who tracks shipments end-to-end, resolves delays, and keeps import-export paperwork compliant.

vnMarket.value: Vietnam's logistics sector pays a wide range depending on company type and specialization: international/3PL companies (e.g. multinational freight forwarders) generally pay more than domestic firms, and English/Mandarin proficiency plus international certifications (APICS CSCP, CILT, FIATA Diploma) or software skills (Oracle TMS, SAP ERP) create bigger income gaps than years of experience alone.

salary.value: Entry-level (0-2 years): 7-12 million VND/month. Import-export/logistics executive level (2-5 years): 12-20 million VND/month. Supply chain specialist: 18-30 million VND/month. Logistics/Supply Chain Manager (5+ years): 35-60 million VND/month. A related overall-average figure reported for similar logistics roles is approximately 16 million VND/month.

demand.value: Recruitment demand in the Logistics/Transportation/Warehousing sector grew 42% year-over-year in Q2 2026, making it one of the fastest-growing hiring sectors in Vietnam's job market that quarter.

similarJobs.name: Warehouse Staff
similarJobs.distinction: Warehouse Staff handles physical receiving, storage, and picking within one site; Logistics Executive coordinates the broader movement of goods across transport, customs, and multiple parties.

similarJobs.name: Import-Export Specialist
similarJobs.distinction: Import-Export Specialist focuses narrowly on trade documentation and customs declarations; Logistics Executive has a broader remit covering shipment tracking, carrier coordination, and cost negotiation in addition to documentation.

similarJobs.name: Supply Chain Planner
similarJobs.distinction: Supply Chain Planner works on demand forecasting and inventory/network planning at a higher, more strategic level; Logistics Executive is operational, executing the day-to-day movement of goods against that plan.

similarJobs.name: Freight Forwarder Agent
similarJobs.distinction: Freight Forwarder Agent typically works for a carrier/forwarding company representing that company's services to shippers; Logistics Executive typically works client-side or in-house, managing the shipper's own logistics operations.

hardSkills.name: Customs & trade documentation
hardSkills.description: Preparing commercial documents and customs declarations, including using systems like VNACCS/VCIS for import-export clearance.

hardSkills.name: Incoterms & trade compliance
hardSkills.description: Applying international trade terms correctly to shipping contracts to avoid cost or liability disputes.

hardSkills.name: WMS/TMS & ERP proficiency
hardSkills.description: Operating warehouse and transport management systems and enterprise systems like SAP ERP to track inventory and shipments.

hardSkills.name: Advanced Excel
hardSkills.description: Using VLOOKUP, pivot tables, and similar functions to reconcile shipment data, costs, and delivery schedules.

hardSkills.name: Freight cost & carrier negotiation
hardSkills.description: Comparing carrier quotes and negotiating rates and terms to control transport costs.

softSkills.name: Cross-team coordination
softSkills.description: Aligning warehouse, transport, customs brokers, and customers so shipments move without handoff delays.

softSkills.name: Problem-solving under time pressure
softSkills.description: Resolving shipment delays, documentation errors, or customs holds quickly to avoid missed deadlines.

softSkills.name: Negotiation
softSkills.description: Securing favorable rates and terms with carriers, vendors, and freight forwarders.

softSkills.name: Attention to detail
softSkills.description: Avoiding costly errors in customs paperwork, quantities, or shipping instructions.

softSkills.name: Adaptability
softSkills.description: Adjusting plans quickly when disruptions occur (port congestion, weather, customs changes).
